title: Cannabis Smoothie Recipe: Easy Infused Blend
h1: A Quick Cannabis-Infused Smoothie, Four Ways
metaDescription: A three-ingredient cannabis smoothie base with two ways to infuse it, tincture or canna-oil, plus berry, tropical, chocolate-banana and green versions.
excerpt: Frozen fruit, milk and yogurt make the base, and one measured tincture dose or spoon of canna-oil makes it infused. Change the flavor, keep the dose.
keyTakeaways: The base is three ingredients: frozen fruit, milk and yogurt. The dose is one measured infusion per glass.
A tincture is the easiest to measure. Canna-oil or cannabutter mixes through best with some fat in the blend, like yogurt or nut butter.
THC or CBD both work. Start low, and wait at least 2 hours before another glass.
Swap the fruit for berry, tropical, chocolate-banana or green versions without changing the dose math.
body:
This cannabis smoothie recipe is a simple formula: frozen fruit, milk and yogurt, plus one measured dose of a THC or CBD tincture or a small spoon of canna-oil. Because the infusion is measured per glass, you can change flavors as often as you like without redoing any math. It's a quick blend for a slow weekend morning or an afternoon at home.

## One measured dose per glass

Whether it's a THC smoothie or a CBD smoothie, make one glass at a time with one measured dose in it. With a tincture, the label gives you a close figure for what went in; with homemade canna-oil, the number is a rougher estimate. If you're new to THC, start small: Health Canada suggests new consumers look for 2.5 mg of THC or less. Our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) explains how to find your amount.

## Tincture or canna-oil?

- **Tincture:** the easiest to measure. Labels list mg per ml, and a marked dropper keeps each dose consistent. Our [cannabis tincture guide](/blog/cannabis-tincture-guide/) covers the basics.
- **Canna-oil or cannabutter:** THC dissolves in fat, not water, so an oil infusion mixes in best when the blend has some fat to carry it. Yogurt, whole milk or nut butter helps. Melt cannabutter first, or it firms into flecks on the frozen fruit. Making your own? Start with our [canna-oil recipe](/blog/canna-oil-recipe/).

Using [infused almond butter](/blog/cannabis-infused-almond-butter/) as your nut butter? Count it as the dose and skip the tincture. And don't expect an indica or sativa label to make a smoothie calming or energizing; research shows those labels don't reliably reflect a plant's genetics. Our [indica vs. sativa guide](/blog/indica-vs-sativa/) explains why.

## How to blend it

Liquid goes in first, then the yogurt and infusion, then the frozen fruit, so the blades catch. Blend a full minute when you use an oil infusion. Thin it with milk or thicken it with ice, taste, and pour.

## Cannabis smoothie recipe variations

Four infused smoothie ideas, each with the same single dose:

| Flavor | Fruit | Good add-ins |
|---|---|---|
| Berry | Mixed berries | A drizzle of honey |
| Tropical | Mango and pineapple | Coconut milk as the liquid |
| Chocolate-banana | Frozen banana | Cocoa powder and peanut butter |
| Green | Banana, pineapple and a handful of spinach | A squeeze of lime |

## Storage and labeling

Drink it fresh, since the infusion can settle as it sits. For meal prep, freeze bags of fruit and add-ins and add the dose when you blend. Or freeze finished single-dose smoothies, each labeled with the cannabinoid, dose and date, on a shelf children and pets can't reach. If someone drinks one by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222.

Looking for a tincture? Check your nearest High Society store's [menu](/shop/) before you go, since selection varies by store. 21+ only. Please consume responsibly.

faq.q: Should I use tincture or canna-oil in a smoothie?
faq.a: Tincture, if precision matters most. It's labeled in mg per ml and disappears into the blend. Canna-oil works well too, especially with yogurt or nut butter to carry it, but homemade oil is always an estimate. Whichever you choose, use one measured dose per glass, never a free pour.

faq.q: Can I use CBD instead of THC?
faq.a: Yes. A CBD tincture goes in the same way, measured by the label. CBD doesn't cause the high that THC does, but check the label's THC figure too, since Michigan's licensed cannabis products list both on the label. If you take any medications, ask your doctor or pharmacist before adding CBD to your routine.

faq.q: How long does an infused smoothie take to work?
faq.a: Expect a wait. An edible may not register for half an hour, sometimes not for two, and it can keep building for up to 4 hours. A rich, fatty blend may land later than you expect: in one study, THC capsules taken after a high-fat meal peaked later, and more THC was absorbed overall. Effects may linger for as long as 12 hours.

ingredients: 1 cup frozen fruit (see the flavor table)
1 measured dose of THC or CBD tincture, or 1 to 2 teaspoons canna-oil or melted cannabutter (see the dosing note)
Optional: 1 tablespoon nut butter or chia seeds
Optional: 1 to 2 teaspoons honey, a drop of vanilla, a few ice cubes
steps: Pour the milk into the blender, then add the yogurt, the measured infusion and any nut butter or seeds.
Add the frozen fruit on top and blend on high for 45 to 60 seconds, until silky. Oil infusions need the full minute.
Check the texture. Add a splash of milk to loosen it or a few ice cubes to thicken it, then blend again.
Taste, sweeten if you like, and pour it all into one glass.
recipe.dosingNote: **One glass, one dose.** With a tincture, ml added × the label's mg per ml = THC in the glass. For example, 0.5 ml of a tincture labeled 5 mg per ml adds about 2.5 mg. With homemade canna-oil, the figure is an estimate that depends on the potency of your starting flower and on losses during decarboxylation and infusion. Start low, wait at least 2 hours before another glass, label anything you store, and keep infused drinks away from children and pets.

sources.label: Health Canada: What you need to know if you choose to consume cannabis
PubChem (U.S. National Library of Medicine): Tetrahydrocannabinol, solubility
Lunn S. et al. (2019), Oral THC pharmacokinetics in fed versus fasted conditions, Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research
Watts S. et al. (2021), Cannabis labelling is associated with genetic variation in terpene synthase genes, Nature Plants
U.S. Food and Drug Administration: What you need to know about products containing cannabis or cannabis-derived compounds, including CBD
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Cannabis frequently asked questions
Michigan Cannabis Regulatory Agency: Marihuana Rules, R 420.1 to R 420.1004 (packaging and labeling)

review.summary: 20 claims checked: 17 ok, 3 overstated (fixed). One supported safety detail added from a cited study; FDA source added for the CBD medication line.

claims.claim: THC dissolves in fat, not water
claims.source: https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/16078 (PUG View Solubility section via the PubChem REST API): 'Essentially insoluble in water'; 'Soluble in fixed oils.'

claims.claim: An oil infusion 'needs' fat in the blend to carry it (body); canna-oil 'needs some fat in the blend' to mix through (takeaway)
claims.fix: now 'mixes in best when the blend has some fat' and 'mixes through best with some fat': fat-rich ingredients help an oil disperse, but nothing shows the blend fails without them
claims.source: reasoning from https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/16078 (oil-soluble, essentially water-insoluble); no study of smoothies

claims.claim: With a tincture 'the label tells you exactly what went in'; 'a marked dropper keeps it exact'
claims.fix: now 'the label gives you a close figure' and 'keeps each dose consistent', with homemade oil 'a rougher estimate'
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-labeling details (R 420.504(1)): labels carry THC and CBD concentration 'with a statement that actual values may vary by 10%'

claims.claim: Health Canada suggests new consumers look for 2.5 mg of THC or less
claims.source: https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-medication/cannabis/resources/what-you-need-to-know-if-you-choose-to-consume-cannabis.html (WebFetch): 'if you are a new consumer, look for a product containing 2.5 mg of THC or less.'

claims.claim: Indica or sativa labels don't reliably reflect a plant's genetics, so don't expect them to make a smoothie calming or energizing
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8516649/ (Watts 2021, abstract via E-utilities, PMID 34650264): 'Sativa- and Indica-labelled samples were genetically indistinct on a genome-wide scale.'

claims.claim: An edible may not register for half an hour, sometimes not for two; it can keep building for up to 4 hours; effects may linger up to 12 hours
claims.source: Health Canada page above: 'It can take 30 minutes to 2 hours after consumption to begin to feel the effects, but up to 4 hours to feel the full effects.'; 'Effects can last up to 12 hours'

claims.claim: In one study, THC taken after a high-fat meal peaked later
claims.fix: kept, now naming the capsules and adding the study's other finding (more THC absorbed overall), so readers do not read 'later' as 'weaker'
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6922062/ (Lunn 2019, abstract via E-utilities, PMID 31872060): 'The presence of high-fat food significantly enhanced time to peak plasma concentration (Tmax) and area under the curve (AUC0-24) for both THC and 11-OH-THC'

claims.claim: CBD doesn't cause the high that THC does
claims.source: Health Canada page above: 'CBD is not intoxicating and may reduce some of the effects of THC; however, it does have an effect on the brain.'

claims.claim: Check a CBD tincture's THC figure too, 'since Michigan labels list both'
claims.fix: now 'since Michigan's licensed cannabis products list both on the label': the labeling rule covers marijuana products from licensed businesses, not every CBD product sold in the state
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-labeling: 'Every marijuana product sold in Michigan must be sealed and labeled with its THC and CBD content' (R 420.504; CRA rules PDF in the sources list)

claims.claim: If you take any medications, ask your doctor or pharmacist before adding CBD
claims.fix: added the FDA page to sources
claims.source: https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/what-you-need-know-and-what-were-working-find-out-about-products-containing-cannabis-or-cannabis (WebFetch): 'Taking CBD with other medications may increase or decrease the effects of the other medications.'; 'Consumer use of any CBD products should always be discussed with a healthcare provider.'

claims.claim: Tincture math: ml × label mg per ml; 0.5 ml of a 5 mg/ml tincture adds about 2.5 mg
claims.source: arithmetic (0.5 × 5 = 2.5)

claims.claim: Homemade canna-oil figure is an estimate that depends on flower potency and decarboxylation and infusion losses
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC REST): 'the conversion of the acid to Δ9-THC was never perfectly complete without loss or degradation of starting material'

claims.claim: Start low and wait at least 2 hours before another glass
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch): 'it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug.'

claims.claim: If someone drinks one by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html: 'call a poison control center at: at 1-800-222-1222.'

claims.claim: Label stored smoothies; keep infused drinks where children and pets can't reach
claims.source: Health Canada page above: store edible cannabis 'securely' and 'out of reach of children, youth, and pets.'

claims.claim: Melt cannabutter first, or it firms into flecks on the frozen fruit
claims.source: physical reasoning: butter is solid at refrigerator temperature and sets on contact with frozen fruit

claims.claim: Drink it fresh, since the infusion can settle as it sits
claims.source: reasoning from PubChem (oil-soluble THC separates from a water-based drink over time); no figure stated

claims.claim: Green version: no detox or health benefit claimed
claims.source: read of the table and body: only fruit, spinach and lime listed (brief mustAvoid respected)

claims.claim: High Society: check your nearest store's menu for a tincture, since selection varies by store
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.productCategories (tinctures on the Birch Run and New Buffalo menus); compliance.responsibleUseLines ('Selection varies—check today's availability.'); no product named as stocked

claims.claim: '21+ only. Please consume responsibly.'
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json compliance.responsibleUseLines (verbatim High Society line)

review.notes: Independent fact-check, 2026-10-24. Health Canada and FDA pages reopened with WebFetch; Lunn 2019 and Watts 2021 abstracts read through NCBI E-utilities; THC solubility read from PubChem's REST API. The writer cited the CDC FAQ for 'CBD is not impairing'; this check did not look for that line on the CDC page and verified the CBD sentence against Health Canada instead. No Michigan law beyond the labeling rule, now scoped to licensed products. High Society: one mention (menu; selection varies), in hs-facts; the shop link sits in the storage section, not near the CBD or onset copy. Writer's notes: No detox or health claim for the green version; no strain-mood promise (brief mustAvoid). Medication line points readers to a clinician without claiming a specific interaction. High Society mentioned once (menu; selection varies, no stock claim).
writerClaims: New consumers: 2.5 mg THC or less; onset 30 min to 2 h, full effect up to 4 h, effects up to 12 h: Health Canada, What you need to know if you choose to consume cannabis.
THC essentially insoluble in water, soluble in fixed oils: PubChem compound 16078, Solubility section.
High-fat meal increased THC exposure (AUC) and delayed Tmax for oral THC capsules: Lunn 2019 abstract.
Sativa- and Indica-labelled samples genetically indistinct genome-wide: Watts 2021 abstract.
CBD is not impairing and does not cause a high; Poison Control 1-800-222-1222: CDC cannabis FAQ.
Michigan labels list THC and CBD concentration: law-facts mi-labeling (R 420.504).
